subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Gate Drivers: Commanding the Switch
description: A quick, practical guide to Gate Drivers: Commanding the Switch.

hook.text: A power switch needs a gate driver — a circuit that charges and discharges the gate fast enough.

buildup.text: The gate is a capacitor. Charging it slowly means the switch lingers in the linear region — wasting power.

discovery.text: High-side drivers need level shifting or isolation — the source terminal floats at high voltage.

twist.text: Bootstrap circuits charge a capacitor when the low-side switch is on, then use that charge to drive the high side.

climax.text: Integrated gate driver ICs handle timing, dead-time, and protection — simplifying design enormously.

punchline.text: Charge the gate fast, protect the switch — the driver is the unsung hero.

quiz.question: Why is driving a high-side switch more challenging than a low-side switch?
options: High-side switches require more current to operate
The source terminal floats at high voltage, requiring level shifting or isolation
High-side switches are physically larger and harder to mount
